A common uncertain transfer law is more defensible than underdetermined catalyst-specific fits.

choice: Use an externally heated multitubular packed fixed-bed reactor with optimized temperature and per-pass conversion at low pressure, with catalyst inventory determined from the transferred net productivity.
alternatives: Adiabatic fixed bed
Fluidized bed
Membrane reactor
Electrically heated microchannel reactor
reason: Ammonia decomposition is strongly endothermic, so distributed external heat avoids the severe temperature fall of an adiabatic bed. Most usable literature records come from fixed-bed flow reactors, minimizing scale-transfer ambiguity. Membrane and microchannel configurations would confound catalyst ranking with proprietary membrane/geometry performance.
evidence: Usable extracted records predominantly report fixed-bed flow tests

choice: Recover unconverted NH3 by refrigerated condensation and knockout for recycle, then purify H2 from N2 by PSA; burn PSA tail hydrogen in the reactor furnace and compress purified H2 to product pressure.
alternatives: No NH3 recycle with once-through near-complete conversion
Cryogenic H2/N2 distillation
Hydrogen-selective membrane reactor
Aqueous acid scrubbing of residual NH3 followed by PSA
reason: The selected train makes conversion economically optimizable: lower per-pass conversion increases ammonia recycle, refrigeration, and equipment duties, while higher conversion approaches equilibrium and increases catalyst/temperature demand. PSA is a conventional route to high-purity compressed hydrogen, and tail-gas firing recovers otherwise lost hydrogen energy without crediting it as purchased energy.

10.18573/jae.33 system paper documents integrated cracking/separation alternatives

choice: Use atomic nitrogen adsorption energy on close-packed transition-metal sites as the descriptor; model NH3 adsorption, three sequential N-H scissions, H2 recombination and N2 recombination with linear adsorbate scaling and BEP barriers, producing a Sabatier volcano between weak-binding N-H activation and strong-binding N2 desorption.
alternatives: d-band center as descriptor

metal nitride vacancy formation energy

reason: Ammonia decomposition activity across transition metals is classically governed by the trade-off between N-H activation and removal of strongly bound nitrogen. A nitrogen-binding descriptor directly links the experimentally discussed nitrogen-removal bottleneck to a tractable microkinetic volcano and can be mapped to metal price.
